title: Give Your World a Lost Civilization
lesson: A lost civilization that is only ancient and mysterious is just rocks. Let its remains say who they were: a tool nobody can make now (technology), the room they built biggest (values), how it ended (failure) and one small trace of an ordinary day. Then leave one question open and never answer it. Every ruin keeps one secret.

voice.direction: The same lab host, quieter this time, like someone walking a dig at dusk. The hook is a mystery stated, not asked. 'Ancient, mysterious, gone' is a dry list of clichés; 'just rocks' lands flat. The rules are crisp, two beats each, with a little wonder on the kitchen and the handprints. 'Half this wall is newer than us' is the chill; 'Nobody has seen them' is almost a whisper. The comment ask is playful.

lines.text: These ruins are older than humans. Someone keeps repairing them.
Meet the Builders. Their wall still stands.
The lazy version: ancient, mysterious, gone.
A thousand years of digging. Nothing but stones.
A ruin that says nothing is just rocks.
Good ruins talk. Four rules. The fifth is the twist.
One: their tools. A gear that nobody here can make.
Two: what they valued. Their biggest room was a kitchen.
Three: how they failed. Every well is full of sand.
Four: their days. A child's handprints, pressed into the mortar.
Run it again. A thousand years. Every find opens two questions.
Rule five? Look closer. Half this wall is newer than us.
Someone replaces one stone every night. Nobody has seen them.
Show how they lived and fell. Every ruin keeps one secret.
What should archaeologists never find in your world?
Part 35 of 50. Follow for part 36: two armies are never enough.

shots.purpose: Close EP34's loop (broken pillars rose on 'the ruins are older than us') and stop the scroll on the mystery.
shots.visual: Golden hour, looking north at a long broken wall of squared stone south of the lake: EP34's pillars stand for good at its east end, the gear's pit, the kitchen and the sand-filled wells lie dug in front of it, and one stone high in the wall is newer than the rest and glows faintly quartz cyan. OLDER THAN US / WHO REPAIRS IT? from frame 0, each line pulsing on its word; the new stone flares on 'repairing' (NEW STONE · LAST NIGHT). Then the field card: THE BUILDERS · LOST CIVILIZATION · LEFT: one wall, still standing.
shots.camera: Frontal (az 0, el 13, fov 20), sliding slowly west along the wall's top.

layers.background: the lake, the valley, the peak

shots.onScreenText: OLDER THAN US / WHO REPAIRS IT? · FIELD CARD NO. 010 · THE BUILDERS
shots.transition: Umber block wipe into the lazy version.
shots.music: Hollow: a blown bottle and vibraphone echoes over a contrabass drone; a hit on 'repairing'.

shots.purpose: The lazy version: ancient, mysterious, gone.
shots.visual: A wipe to the bare wall: nothing dug in front of it, no new stone, nothing to read. ANCIENT / MYSTERIOUS / GONE pop on their words. The finds tray slides in under the world, EMPTY; the sim bar arrives (FINDS 00, QUESTIONS 00) and RUN is pressed.
shots.camera: The same frontal pose, sliding east along the bare wall.
shots.onScreenText: ANCIENT · MYSTERIOUS · GONE · THE FINDS TRAY: EMPTY
shots.transition: A cut to the whole Isle on 'run'.

shots.purpose: Run the lazy version: a thousand years of digging and nothing to find.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; YEAR 500→1500; the tray stays EMPTY. 1,000 YEARS / OF DIGGING / JUST STONES.
shots.camera: Wide (dist 160, fov 22), sliding east across the Isle.

shots.purpose: The punchline: a ruin that says nothing is just rocks.
shots.visual: Gloom: JUST ROCKS · 0 FINDS · 0 QUESTIONS · 0 PEOPLE, over the empty tray.
shots.camera: Wide, the slide easing to a stop.

shots.purpose: Re-hook: the thesis, four rules, one locked.
shots.visual: REWIND. GOOD RUINS / TALK; then the checklist READ THE RUINS, row 5 locked (the twist); the tray's fifth compartment is locked too.
shots.onScreenText: GOOD RUINS TALK · READ THE RUINS 0/5
shots.transition: Cut to the wall's west end.
shots.music: Survey, bare (a nylon guitar walking in eighths); a riser into 'the twist'.

shots.visual: The wall's west end: on 'gear' a toothed bronze wheel rises half out of a dug pit (FIND 01 · TOOLS · NO FORGE HERE) and drops into the tray's first compartment.
shots.camera: Cut, then the slide begins: the camera trucks east to the gear.
shots.onScreenText: 1 TOOLS · a gear we can't make

shots.visual: Sliding east: on 'biggest' a great room's foundations rise in front of the wall, one long table for everyone, benches, bowls and a hearth with a great pot (FIND 02 · VALUES · ONE TABLE FOR ALL).
shots.camera: A slide east along the wall (no cut).

shots.visual: Sliding east: on 'well' two stone wells rise, each filled to the brim with sand, sand drifting against the wall (FIND 03 · FAILURE · THE WATER RAN OUT).
shots.onScreenText: 3 A FAILURE · wells full of sand

shots.visual: Sliding east and in to the wall's face: on 'child's' a mortar patch with two small handprints shows on a low block (FIND 04 · DAILY LIFE · A CHILD WAS HERE).
shots.camera: A slide east that eases in to the wall's face (el 8).

shots.purpose: Run with the remains talking: a thousand years of digging, and every find opens two questions.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; YEAR 500→1500; pits open round the site one after another; FINDS 4→16 and QUESTIONS 4→32; in the tray every find sprouts two question marks. MORE QUESTIONS · 1,000 YEARS · 16 FINDS · 32 QUESTIONS, stamped in quartz.
shots.music: Drive with the theme; a stab and a cymbal on 'questions'.

shots.purpose: The locked rule: half this wall is newer than us.
shots.visual: Dusk, the whole wall: RULE 5? LOOK CLOSER; on 'Half' the repair log lights: every original stone sinks to umber and every repair glows quartz cyan by how recent it is, half the wall (THE REPAIR LOG · HALF OF IT IS NEW; NEWER THAN US). Night falls; the camera slides to the gap at the top of the wall, and on 'night' one more stone settles into it, bright (LAST NIGHT · ONE MORE STONE); nobody is there (WHO? · NOBODY SEEN). The tray's fifth compartment opens: WHO? · no answer.
shots.camera: Cut, then slides east along the wall to the gap.

layers.midground: the glowing repairs, the new stone

shots.onScreenText: RULE 5? LOOK CLOSER · NEWER THAN US · THE REPAIR LOG · LAST NIGHT · WHO?
shots.music: Twist (a held A7♭9), then hollow at night with the theme on the blown bottle.

shots.visual: Day returns and the log fades; the checklist opens and row 5 unlocks on 'who': A SECRET · never say who · 5/5. The follow chip (+ FOLLOW · PART 35/50) after 'who'.
shots.camera: A slide east along the wall.
shots.music: Anthem from 'So'; a D-major hit on 'who'.

shots.visual: The full card (BEFORE YOU BURY A CIVILIZATION · THE BUILDERS, all five rows ticked) over the whole Isle in golden light, with 'Every ruin keeps one secret.' in serif italic from the end of the first sentence.
shots.onScreenText: BEFORE YOU BURY A CIVILIZATION · THE BUILDERS · Every ruin keeps one secret.
shots.transition: Block wipe to the end card.
shots.music: Anthem; the World Engine chime as the card lands.

shots.purpose: Comment CTA: what should archaeologists never find in your world?
shots.visual: End card: logo, PART 35 / 50, the title, and a COMMENT panel where OUR OWN NAMES and A WARM HEARTH pop as starters, then 'One find. Name it.'
shots.camera: Cut (under the block wipe) to the hook pose, sliding back onto it.
shots.onScreenText: COMMENT · OUR OWN NAMES / A WARM HEARTH · One find. Name it.

graphics.title: Give Your World a Lost Civilization

shots.purpose: Say the part number, ask for the follow with a reason (part 36), open the next loop.
shots.visual: The hook frame; PART 35/50; FOLLOW FOR PART 36, pressed on 'Follow'; NEXT RUN · 36 decodes from three locked banners to THE WAR · MORE THAN TWO SIDES. In the world, on 'armies', three standards in three colours rise on three meadows behind the wall and the war horn calls; the Queen looks up; they sink back before the hook title returns.

layers.foreground: progress bar, follow button, next-run card

shots.onScreenText: PART 35/50 · FOLLOW FOR PART 36 · NEXT RUN: THE WAR · MORE THAN TWO SIDES.
shots.music: Tease over a held A; a horn call on 'armies'; the engine chime on 'Follow'.

music.key: D minor, resolving to D major

youtube.description:
These ruins are older than humans. Someone keeps repairing them.

Meet the Builders: their wall still stands. The lazy version of a lost civilization is ancient, mysterious and gone, and we ran it: a thousand years of digging, nothing but stones. A ruin that says nothing is just rocks.

Good ruins talk. Their tools: a gear that nobody here can make. What they valued: their biggest room was a kitchen. How they failed: every well is full of sand. Their days: a child's handprints, pressed into the mortar. Run it again: a thousand years, and every find opens two questions.

Then the twist: look closer. Half this wall is newer than us. Someone replaces one stone every night, and nobody has seen them. So never tell us who.

Show how they lived and fell. Every ruin keeps one secret.

What is the one thing archaeologists should never find in your world?

Part 35 of 50. Follow for part 36: two armies are never enough.

Worldcraft Shorts: Worldbuilding, from the ground up. Season 2, The World Engine: every idea gets tested on one living island. Arc 7: History and Mythology (the arc's last episode). The Builders, their wall and everything found in it are invented for this video; no real civilization, ruin or script is depicted.
